reconcile.note: The Geneva Bible annotators distinguish God's fixed decree from an announced threatening, which always carries a condition, leaving prophecy's sureness untouched.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Robert P. Carroll catalogues this as a contradiction, but the project's public-domain source survey found no verbatim critic passage that engages it.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Robert P. Carroll, When Prophecy Failed: Reactions and Responses to Failure in the Old Testament Prophetic Traditions (1979).

sides.snippet: if that nation, concerning which I have spoken, turn from their evil, I will repent of the evil that I thought to do to them.
sides.verseText: if that nation, concerning which I have spoken, turn from their evil, I will repent of the evil that I thought to do to them.

sides.snippet: We have the more sure word of prophecy; whereunto you do well that you take heed, as to a lamp shining in a dark place
sides.verseText: We have the more sure word of prophecy; whereunto you do well that you take heed, as to a lamp shining in a dark place, until the day dawns, and the day star arises in your hearts:
